Origin, date_confidence, n_editions and author productivity are about balanced across the two periods. The effect holds within each date-confidence group (high-confidence dates +0.054, medium +0.058, low +0.039) and within each origin (UK +0.054, US +0.076, unknown +0.044). An OLS model adjusting for genre, origin, date_confidence, log editions and log author productivity, with SEs clustered by author, gives +0.051 [0.034, 0.068]. By decade the rate is about 0.04-0.06 from the 1850s to 1870s and about 0.11-0.12 from the 1880s on. That looks like a step up around the cutoff, though the decades before 1850 are small and noisy. Caveats: the early period is thin (about 880 works), and some early genre cells have fewer than 60 works, with two early cells at a rate of 0. The labels come from an annotator or classifier and could drift with period language. Each work contributes only one sampled passage. The cited passage IDs are high-confidence-dated passages tagged DISTANCE_TRAVEL from both periods. They show what the construct looks like but do not by themselves establish the trend."
